name: Knowledge Architecture
tagline: A typed knowledge system that humans and coding agents share.
description: A specification and a Python linter for knowledge shared by humans and coding agents. It separates operational instructions, evidence, beliefs, decisions, and current work, with explicit authority and review rules. The standard-library CLI validates documentation, scaffolds a minimal setup, and checks decision changes in pull requests.
highlights: Published v0.1.2 with immutable release tags and matching adoption documents and linter downloads.
The v0.1.2 release includes 82 tests covering initialization, Markdown links, metadata, decision graphs, and review gates.
GitHub CI runs tests and strict lint on Python 3.10 and 3.12, plus separate checks for decision acceptance, protected edits, and removal.
Initialization creates a shared protocol hub and tool pointers, preserves an existing README, and avoids empty documentation directories.
The published v0.1.2 download was verified against its tag and tested through initialization and strict lint.

story.why: Teams were copying long Markdown lists for coding agents and then maintaining a second copy per tool, so protocol, beliefs, decisions, and scratch mixed and no agent could tell what was true.
story.problem: Improvised AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, wikis, and TODO files create conflicting instructions, empty ceremony directories, and files that agents treat as facts.
challenges: Keep operational instructions in AGENTS.md while using thin compatibility pointers for other agent entrypoints.
Distinguish a proposed decision from a human-approved constraint, and require separate review for acceptance, edits, and removal.
Keep copied linter versions and adoption instructions compatible without silently changing published artifacts.
Combine pull-request checks with branch protection while acknowledging that repository administrators retain bypass permissions.
Catch mechanical errors without claiming that a linter can judge evidence quality, mixed information kinds, or human intent.
designDecisions: Keep canonical knowledge as Markdown and small scripts in Git.
Use MIT licensing for the specification, prompts, and linter.
Maintain one operational hub in AGENTS.md; tool entrypoints point to it instead of duplicating its rules.
Create documentation only when it has real content; initialization builds only the minimal setup.
Keep published tags immutable and distinguish development versions from the last published download.
Require separate human-accepted, human-edited, and human-removed labels for decision changes, as approved in ADR 0003.
Preserve the v0.1.x JSON result contract and retain strict freshness checks.

future.next: Maintain the verified v0.1.2 release and use adopter feedback to decide whether further changes are needed. Adopter listings are not evidence of completed field validation.
roadmap: Review the dated agent-compatibility table before 2026-11-17.
Use adopter field reports to guide further specification and linter changes.
Keep published releases immutable and validate documentation and linter compatibility before the next release.
upcomingFeatures: Follow-up fixes supported by adopter feedback.
ideas: Evaluate a package-based install path if adopters need it.
Add local search only when a source wiki outgrows a readable index.
Explore additional mechanical checks without treating them as substitutes for human review.
